    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The industrial sector could produce some of the market's biggest winners in 2027, particularly among companies supplying the equipment and infrastructure needed to meet America's growing electricity demand.
    • Quanta Services is positioned to benefit from the construction of new transmission networks, while Eaton supplies the electrical equipment needed for those projects.
    • Recent findings suggest that all three have substantial opportunities extending into the coming year, supported by existing orders and multiyear infrastructure investments.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jeff Siegel – Nov 20, 2026 at 9:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vertiv ›.

    The industrial sector could produce some of the market's biggest winners in 2027, particularly among companies supplying the equipment and infrastructure needed to meet America's growing electricity demand. Three companies I'd put near the top of that list are Quanta Services (PWR -2.07%), Eaton (ETN -1.68%), and Vertiv Holdings (VRT -3.99%).

    Quanta Services is positioned to benefit from the construction of new transmission networks, while Eaton supplies the electrical equipment needed for those projects. Meanwhile, Vertiv stands to benefit as new AI data centers require increasingly sophisticated power management and cooling systems.

    Recent findings suggest that all three have substantial opportunities extending into the coming year, supported by existing orders and multiyear infrastructure investments. And while their valuations could limit returns, continued spending on these projects gives all three a credible chance of outperforming the broader market in 2027.

    In a recent development, quanta Services builds and maintains the infrastructure that delivers electricity and natural gas. Its work includes transmission lines, substations, pipelines, and other infrastructure needed to support the expansion of power demand.

    Recent findings suggest that in Q3 2026, Quanta reported revenue of $12.01 billion, up approximately 57% from $7.63 billion a year earlier. Adjusted earnings per share jumped 82%, from $3.33 to $6.06.

    Sources indicate that meanwhile, its total backlog reached a record $63.7 billion, providing considerable visibility into future revenue. Management subsequently raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to between $41.3 billion and $41.6 billion, with adjusted earnings per share expected to reach $17.90 to $18.30.

    NYSE · As of 9:58 AM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, quanta's key advantage is its ability to handle large, complicated infrastructure projects. Utilities need additional transmission capacity, data centers require reliable electricity connections, and aging electrical systems need upgrades. These projects can take years to complete, potentially supporting revenue well beyond 2027.

    The risks, however, include labor shortages, project delays, and a valuation that may already reflect substantial future growth. But Quanta's backlog and earnings momentum make it a very strong industrial stock play.

    Industry observers note that eaton manufactures electrical equipment used to manage, distribute, and protect power. Its products are essential components in data centers, factories, commercial buildings, and utility infrastructure.

    In Q3, revenue reached a record $8.9 billion, increasing 28% year over year. Organic revenue growth, which excludes acquisitions and currency fluctuations, reached 19%, and adjusted earnings per share climbed to $3.68, while segment operating margins reached a record 25.3%. Demand is also accelerating.

    Industry observers note that eaton reported that its electrical businesses experienced a 46% year-over-year increase in total backlog. Meanwhile, rolling 12-month organic orders increased by 39% in Electrical Americas and 51% in Electrical Global. Those numbers suggest customers are continuing to invest heavily in electrical infrastructure.

    Management expects full-year 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $13.70 to $13.80. The tech giant is also expanding manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand.

    NYSE · As of 9:55 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Overall, Eaton's biggest advantage is its exposure to multiple industries. It benefits from data center construction, but also serves utilities, manufacturers, aerospace customers, and commercial facilities. That diversification could help sustain growth even if spending in one market slows.

    Sources indicate that as artificial intelligence drives demand for more powerful computing systems, data centers require increasingly sophisticated cooling and electrical equipment. Vertiv is benefiting directly from that spending.

    Industry observers note that third-quarter revenue reached $4.31 billion, increasing 61% year over year. Organic revenue growth, which excludes acquisitions, reached 55%. Meanwhile, adjusted earnings per share jumped 78% to $2.21, while adjusted operating profit increased 83% to approximately $1.09 billion.

    Organic orders more than doubled compared with the same quarter a year earlier, and the organization also generated $652 million in adjusted free cash flow during the quarter, an increase of 50%.

    Management subsequently raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to between $14.45 billion and $14.85 billion. Adjusted earnings per share are expected to reach $7.10 to $7.20, representing approximately 69% to 71% growth. Those numbers suggest Vertiv could enter 2027 with substantial momentum.

    NYSE · As of 9:56 AM ET 11/20/26.

    However, the stock carries considerable risk. Its rapid growth has attracted significant investor enthusiasm, and any slowdown in data center spending could pressure both earnings expectations and its valuation.

    Of these three companies, Vertiv could deliver the strongest earnings growth in 2027. But I'd be careful about assuming that translates into the biggest stock gains.

    Sources indicate that quanta's record backlog offers visibility into future infrastructure spending, while Eaton's diversified electrical business provides exposure to several growing markets. Vertiv has the fastest recent earnings growth but potentially the greatest sensitivity to shifting expectations around AI infrastructure spending.

    It has been revealed that my prediction is that all three will benefit from continued investment in electrical infrastructure during 2027. The biggest winner, however, may be the tech giant that delivers earnings growth exceeding what Wall Street has already priced into its shares.

    • As digital transformation continues to sweep through the global financial landscape, investors are comparing Robinhood Markets (HOOD -0.60%) and Nu (NU +0.72%) to see which stock offers the best growth potential through 2027.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Erin Kennedy – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 9:55AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Robinhood Markets ›.

    As digital transformation continues to sweep through the global financial landscape, investors are comparing Robinhood Markets (HOOD -0.60%) and Nu (NU +0.72%) to see which stock offers the best growth potential through 2027.

    Robinhood disrupted the domestic brokerage industry by democratizing access to trading and cryptocurrency for millions of users. Nu is a dominant digital bank in Latin America, providing low-cost financial services to a massive, underserved population. Both companies represent a shift away from traditional banking toward mobile-first, technology-driven financial ecosystems.

    Industry observers note that robinhood provides a multifaceted platform for retail investors, offering stocks, Bitcoin (BTC -3.67%), and digital banking services. It recently expanded into institutional-grade services and introduced a credit card to deepen its relationship with users. According to its latest annual report, the manufacturer relies on partners like Amazon (AMZN +0.51%) for cloud infrastructure and Morningstar (MORN +1.99%) for research data.

    Sources indicate that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $5.1 billion, an increase of roughly 21.1%. The company reported net income of approximately $2 billion during this time frame. This performance reflects a significant stabilization in its business model compared to previous years when trading volumes were more volatile.

    Industry observers note that as of Robinhood's December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was about 1.3. This ratio measures how much debt a firm uses relative to the value owned by shareholders. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $1.6 billion. Free cash flow is the cash left over after a company pays for its operations and capital expenditures.

    Industry observers note that nu operates as a digital-first bank, providing credit cards, personal loans, and savings accounts to millions of customers. It focuses on underbanked populations in Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, using lower overhead costs to offer better rates than traditional incumbents. The firm's rapid expansion has made it one of the largest financial institutions in its region.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended June 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $19.4 billion, an increase of approximately 53.2%. Net income for the period was roughly $3.6 billion. This growth highlights the scale of the digital banking shift occurring across emerging markets as owners move away from physical branch locations.

    As of Nu's December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was about 0.5, and the current ratio was roughly 0.6. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $3.5 billion, providing capital to fund further international expansion.

    Robinhood Markets faces significant regulatory and legal uncertainty regarding its payment for order flow practices and the classification of its event contracts. These legal challenges, which include scrutiny from state gaming regulators, could impact its future revenue streams. Additionally, the manufacturer is highly dependent on third parties like Amazon for its underlying cloud technology infrastructure.

    Nu faces risks associated with operating in emerging markets, where economic volatility and currency fluctuations can impact its reported results. The organization must also manage credit risks as it expands its lending products to a broader customer base during different economic cycles. Since it operates as a bank, it is subject to rigorous capital requirements and oversight by various international financial regulators.

    While Nu offers a significantly lower forward P/E multiple, Robinhood carries a higher premium that reflects its diverse expansion into different financial services and trading asset classes.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    Sources indicate that the P/B ratio compares the stock price with the company's book value, which represents its assets minus its liabilities. Investors frequently use this metric to evaluate bank stocks. A lower P/B ratio indicates that a stock is less expensive relative to its paper value.

    Neither of these stocks is something I'd normally invest in, because I'm a pretty conservative investor. Nu does not appeal to me given my past negative experiences with emerging market stocks (once bitten, twice shy). I don't find Robinhood attractive because at a previous publication I worked at, we rated brokerages. Robinhood was consistently low-scoring, and customers were not shy about saying so. In particular, respondents reported that it has poor customer service. Contrast that with a competitor like Schwab (SCHW +0.55%), which has online chat (with real people), a phone line, and even physical branches. And while Robinhood may have pioneered commission-free trading, that's table stakes now.

    Both of these companies went public in 2021. Let's see how their stocks have performed since:.

    According to recent reports, nu does not compare favorably here; its stock hasn't even kept pace with inflation. Robinhood has delivered a strong performance, but it's seen a fair amount of volatility along the way. Of course, past performance is no indication of future results. But if I had to choose between these two, my vote would be for Robinhood.

    • Industry observers note that kimberly-Clark (KMB +2.37%) closed its acquisition of Kenvue, a consumer health organization spun off from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ +1.19%), on Nov.
    • The deal was valued at $48.7 billion, and Kimberly-Clark expects Kenvue to offer $2.1 billion in merger-related savings and revenue gains.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Nov 20, 2026 at 10:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Kimberly-Clark ›.

    Industry observers note that kimberly-Clark (KMB +2.37%) closed its acquisition of Kenvue, a consumer health organization spun off from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ +1.19%), on Nov. 2.

    The deal was valued at $48.7 billion, and Kimberly-Clark expects Kenvue to offer $2.1 billion in merger-related savings and revenue gains. That sounds good, but management still has to prove Kenvue is a value driver rather than just an expensive acquisition.

    Sources indicate that kimberly-Clark has brands found in homes across the world, including Kleenex, Huggies, and Cottonelle. Adding Kenvue's product portfolio to its lineup seems like a strong fit, as those are also items people generally don't think twice about reaching for when they need them. Kenvue's offerings include the brands Tylenol, Neutrogena, Listerine, and Band-Aid.

    "This transaction brings together two iconic American companies to create a combined portfolio of complementary products, including 10 billion-dollar brands, that touch nearly half the global population through every stage of life," Kimberly-Clark stated in a press release.

    In a recent development, interestingly enough, the main appeal of the deal may not be sales contributions. While Kimberly-Clark expects $2.1 billion in synergies (reinvesting $300 million), only $500 million of that is incremental profit expected to be obtained within the first four years after the acquisition closed.

    The bulk of the acquisition's value lies in cost savings, which could be worth $1.9 billion and could be achieved within the first three years after the acquisition. Compared to those revenue assumptions, lower costs and higher margins will be easier to spot in quarterly reports.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:54 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Everything looks good on paper, but there's a difference between projections and execution. Kenvue was spun off from Johnson & Johnson in 2023, allowing the legacy brand to focus more on high-growth areas.

    Kenvue may ultimately be a better fit for Kimberly-Clark's portfolio than for Johnson & Johnson's. But there's no guarantee that the synergies Kimberly-Clark expects will take shape.

    According to recent reports, also, as Kimberly-Clark shared, the $2.1 billion figure mentioned earlier will take a few years to reach. But over the next several quarters, we'll start to get early previews of how successful the acquisition may be through margins, cost savings, debt levels, and cash flow.

    Recent findings suggest that it's too early to say whether Kimberly-Clark is a buy based solely on the Kenvue acquisition. But as it stands, it's a solid business that has seemingly grown even stronger thanks to the new brands it just acquired. Plus, while shareholders wait, Kimberly-Clark pays out a dividend currently yielding 4.7%.

    #4149. 49ers and Vikings are preparing for Mexico City's thin air in very different ways. Science favors one

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1552 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    49ers and Vikings are preparing for Mexico City's thin air in very different ways. Science favors one

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1552 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan remembers how he felt during college when he returned to visit his parents in Denver after spending a few months at sea level.
    • Recent findings suggest that "You'd run up the stairs and be out of breath," Shanahan told reporters last week.
    • That experience helps explain how Shanahan is preparing San Francisco for Sunday night's high-stakes matchup against the Minnesota Vikings inside Mexico City's famed Estadio Azteca.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan remembers how he felt during college when he returned to visit his parents in Denver after spending a few months at sea level.

    Recent findings suggest that "You'd run up the stairs and be out of breath," Shanahan told reporters last week. "It takes some time to get used to it. It just is what it is with altitude.".

    That experience helps explain how Shanahan is preparing San Francisco for Sunday night's high-stakes matchup against the Minnesota Vikings inside Mexico City's famed Estadio Azteca. The 49ers are spending the entire week training at altitude comparable to what awaits them at the highest-elevation venue ever to host an NFL game.

    According to recent reports, after hanging 46 points on the beleaguered Dallas Cowboys defense last Sunday in Arlington, Texas, the 49ers flew directly to Colorado Springs to begin acclimating to elevation. They are the latest in a long line of NFL teams to practice 7,258 feet above sea level at the Air Force Academy in advance of playing at 7,352-foot Azteca.

    Industry observers note that "It's definitely nicer to play when you're acclimated to the altitude so you're not as out of breath," Shanahan said. "It's rarely the difference in winning or losing, but anything that helps.".

    It has been revealed that as the 49ers practiced against the backdrop of the Rocky Mountains this week, the Vikings tried to bring Mexico City to the Midwest. They erected a massive altitude chamber at their Eagan practice facility that simulates the low-pressure environment found at elevations as high as 12,000 feet.

    Over the past five weeks, Vikings players have subjected themselves to aerobic workouts inside the chamber, using treadmills and stationary bikes to simulate the demands of exercising at altitude. The Vikings hope that altitude training inside their own building reduces the shock factor they experience Sunday night, Tyler Williams, the team's vice president of player health and performance, told reporters in Minnesota on Wednesday.

    "Nearly our whole roster has done five-plus sessions and nearly our whole roster has [experienced] 12,000 feet," Williams added.

    A general view of Estadio Atzeca, in Mexico City, ahead of the 2026 NFL Mexico City game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings.

    The strikingly different approaches taken by the 49ers and Vikings have captured the attention of exercise physiologists who study how athletes prepare to compete at altitude. Those who spoke with Yahoo Sports largely prefer the 49ers' approach, though they acknowledge that there are pros and cons to both teams' methods.

    "The 49ers are doing the right thing spending time at comparable altitude," stated Benjamin Levine, a physiologist and University of Texas Southwestern professor who has co-authored several groundbreaking studies on the effects of altitude on athletes.

    Grégoire Millet, an exercise physiologist at the Institute of Sports Science in Lausanne, Switzerland, agrees that acclimatizing on site or at a similar altitude is "the most effective approach.".

    "Pre-acclimatization in a chamber is better than nothing," Millet remarked, "but does not allow a full acclimatization to altitude.".

    In a recent development, for athletes adjusting to elevation, the primary challenge is that each gulp of thin air delivers less oxygen to their lungs. Their hearts beat faster, their breathing becomes more labored and they tire sooner. They may also need longer to recover between sprints or short bursts of energy.

    If an athlete is training for a major competition at high altitude, exercise physiologists advise them to begin their preparation months in advance. Athletes might train at home using an altitude simulator to expose their bodies to reduced oxygen levels and get in the best possible shape. Then they also often arrive on site 2-3 weeks before the competition starts to give their bodies time to produce extra red blood cells to carry oxygen to the muscles and bolster their endurance.

    Recent findings suggest that that sort of preparation is not realistic for an NFL team traveling to Estadio Azteca for a single game in the midst of an 18-week regular season. The NFC West-leading 49ers (8-1) and NFC North co-leading Vikings (7-2) only have a week to prepare for a showdown that could serve as a preview of the conference championship game.

    Increased red blood cell production may not be feasible that swiftly, but experts say the 49ers should still benefit from spending a week in conditions mimicking what they'll endure at Estadio Azteca.

    "Having a few days of acclimatization helps everything," Levine said. "It helps your endurance. It helps you get through the period where sleep is disrupted and fatigue and dehydration are common. It gets you over acute mountain sickness. I think that's the way to go.".

    Recent findings suggest that the other advantage for the 49ers is having more practice time to recalibrate to how differently the ball moves through air that is less dense. Quarterbacks adjusting to thin air can sail passes over receivers' heads, while field goals and punts also travel farther because of decreased air resistance.

    "The 49ers probably have noticed that this week in their training and readjusted a bit, whereas the Vikings will have quite a shock when they arrive," stated Laura Lewis, the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency's science director and an expert in sport physiology at high altitude. "They'll kind of be learning in their warmup or on the fly, so you might see some crazy passes that make you wonder if they've ever thrown a ball before.".

    NFL players have experience playing at altitude in Denver, but Lewis cautions that the difference in how the ball behaves at 5,280 feet and at 7,352 feet is "notable." As she puts it, "it just compounds the higher that you get.".

    The Vikings' altitude chamber won't help their skill-position players adjust to how the football travels, but Kevin O'Connell's team did have the benefit of sleeping in their own beds all week. Whereas the 49ers are now nearing the end of a two-week, three-city road trip, the Vikings are treating Sunday like a typical road game and won't even have to leave the Central Time Zone.

    Industry observers note that "That's where I would caution the 49ers a little bit, just because now all of a sudden you're on this extended road trip," said Andrew Subudhi, chair of the department of human physiology at the University of Colorado Colorado Springs. "These players are not with their families. They're not sleeping in their own beds. They're outside of their routine. And you've put them at altitude. Many people struggle to sleep even at 6,000 or 7,000 feet. So you can get some cumulative effects from fatigue and travel if the players decide they're kind of over it.".

    In 2017, the New England Patriots were the first NFL team to train at the Air Force Academy ahead of a game in Mexico City. Other teams followed their blueprint after New England overwhelmed the Oakland Raiders 33-8.

    Industry observers note that the Los Angeles Rams did it ahead of a 2018 matchup against Kansas City, only for the NFL to move the game to the LA Coliseum amid concerns about the condition of the Azteca field. A year later, the Los Angeles Chargers prepared in Colorado Springs for their Mexico City game but lost 24-17 to Kansas City. In 2022, the 49ers followed the same travel itinerary they have this week and demolished Arizona, 38-10.

    This is the second time this season that the 49ers have taken a creative approach to preparing to play on international soil.

    San Francisco flew to Melbourne, Australia, a full week ahead of their season opener against the Rams to give players and coaches as long as possible to recharge after a long travel day and adjust to the 17-hour time difference. Los Angeles flew into Melbourne the day before the game and flew out soon after the final whistle, theorizing there would be no need for body clocks to adapt if the trip was as short as possible.

    Treating the longest trip in NFL history like a hit-and-run mission proved disastrous for the Rams. They lost 27-7, head coach Sean McVay admitting a few days later that his travel strategy had backfired.

    Recent findings suggest that "Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn. And sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that put you in a bad spot," McVay said, drawing a laugh from a roomful of reporters.

    Industry observers note that are the Vikings making a similar mistake by not practicing at elevation? Might the 49ers gain a slight advantage once more from a more carefully considered travel plan? Exercise physiologists do seem to prefer San Francisco's plan, but they're quick to point out that playing at altitude will still be a challenge for both teams.

    Pre-game rest and hydration will be a factor. So will depth along the offensive and defensive line, allowing coaches to rotate players when the starters need a rest.

    Ultimately, Subudhi believes that the 49ers' teamwide buy-in might be the most key factor.

    According to recent reports, "The fact that the 49ers have done this in the past and they beat the Cardinals, that's a substantial advantage," Subudhi said. "Whether it physiologically makes sense or not, their coaches and players probably believe, yeah, this is the right way to do it.".

    #4146. Tech Report: Here's the Average Social Security Benefit by Age From 62 to 80

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (587 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Here's the Average Social Security Benefit by Age From 62 to 80

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (587 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 10:00AM EST.
    • According to recent reports, social Security was designed to function as supplemental income.
    • The Social Security Administration (SSA) calculates your benefit based on your earnings across your 35 highest-earning years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 10:00AM EST.

    According to recent reports, social Security was designed to function as supplemental income. It replaces about 40% of your pre-retirement pay, a share that is well short of what most retirees need to cover their costs. But how much you get depends on individual factors.

    The Social Security Administration (SSA) calculates your benefit based on your earnings across your 35 highest-earning years. Full retirement age (FRA) ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later. Your final check depends heavily on the age you choose to start collecting.

    In a recent development, here is the average monthly retired-worker benefit by age, as of December 2025, the most recent data available. These figures reflect the population of retirees at each age today, not the amount you're guaranteed if you claim at that age.

    The age-70 average is roughly 59.7% higher than the age-62 average, a monthly gap of $850.28 or $10,203.36 per year. This climb occurs because claiming at 62, with a full retirement age of 67, results in a permanent 30% reduction. Waiting until 70 adds delayed retirement credits worth 8% for each year you wait past full retirement age.

    After age 70, average benefits plateau and even start to decline. This is not a benefit cut for individuals. Older groups likely include more people who claimed early and locked in lower checks. Women also make up a larger share of the oldest groups because they live longer on average. They often have lower lifetime earnings due to the gender pay gap and time out of the workforce for caregiving.

    Sources indicate that even at the age-70 peak, the average monthly benefit of $2,274.68 ($27,296.16 annually) leaves a large gap in a household budget. The average senior household spends $61,432 in 2024, according to the most recent Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data. This results in a $34,135.84 annual shortfall that retirees must cover through other means.

    A 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will take effect in 2027. It will add about $82 a month on top of the age-70 average, though these snapshot figures don't yet include it. The most useful number on the table is the row that matches your planned claiming age, not the peak for 70-year-olds.

    Industry observers note that the ideal Social Security claiming age for you depends on your finances, life expectancy, and personal preferences. Those with short life expectancies often get a larger lifetime benefit by applying early, while those with average or above-average life expectancies may do better by delaying their application, possibly until age 70 when they qualify for their largest checks.

    If you're married, talk your decision over with your spouse, as it may affect them, too. You cannot claim a spousal benefit on your partner's work record until they are already claiming retirement checks. If your goal is to maximize your household income, it can help to coordinate your claiming ages.

    For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An updated development roadmap and heavy share dilution from a Greenland mining acquisition sent Critical Metals (CRML -2.89%) tumbling 28.7% this week, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence.
    • Recent findings suggest that critical Metals stock changed hands at $3.48 as of the close on Thursday, Nov.
    • Critical Metals completed its acquisition of European Lithium on Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Scott Levine – Nov 20, 2026 at 10:07AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Critical Metals ›.

    An updated development roadmap and heavy share dilution from a Greenland mining acquisition sent Critical Metals (CRML -2.89%) tumbling 28.7% this week, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

    Recent findings suggest that critical Metals stock changed hands at $3.48 as of the close on Thursday, Nov. 19, down 28.7% from Friday, Nov. 13's close through Thursday, Nov. 19's close. Across those five sessions, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.06%) fell 5.1%, and the Nasdaq-100 was down 5.1%.

    Critical Metals completed its acquisition of European Lithium on Nov. 5, taking full control of the Tanbreez rare-earth project in Greenland and raising its post-closing cash balance to $264.5 million. However, issuing roughly 90.5 million new shares to fund the transaction increased the total share count to 194.2 million, resulting in substantial dilution for existing equity holders. Pressure on the stock mounted after an analyst downgrade at peer USA Rare Earth (USAR +1.60%) triggered a broad retreat across rare-earth developers, leaving the stock down 84.1% (as of the close on Thursday, Nov. 19) from its 52-week high.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:56 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Critical Metals is a pre-revenue mineral development company advancing the Tanbreez rare-earth project in Greenland, with no commercial sales yet, meaning its value depends entirely on securing project financing and building mine infrastructure. The business aims to supply heavy rare-earth elements to Western industrial and defense customers looking to bypass concentrated global supply chains. But with initial ore extraction at Tanbreez targeted for late 2028 at the earliest, commercial revenues remain several years away.

    In a recent development, mining megaprojects demand huge upfront capital expenditures for environmental studies, site permitting, and refinery infrastructure. Without current revenue, failing to secure non-dilutive debt or government grants could force further equity raises, creating a high risk of permanent capital loss for existing shareholders. This week's updates flip the focus from acquiring the Tanbreez deposit to managing massive capital needs and share dilution before commercial production begins.

    In a recent development, with no commercial revenue, it's difficult to apply a strict multiple comparison here, as early-stage mining developers trade on asset scale and development milestones rather than sales multiples. Critical Metals now has a market cap of $675.9 million, backed by $264.5 million in cash and short-term investments as of its post-merger patch, providing initial liquidity to advance engineering work. The most critical event for investors to monitor is the definitive feasibility study expected in late 2027, which will establish the project's true economic parameters and long-term funding requirements.

    Sources indicate that investors may find the analyst's downgrade of USA Rare Earth disheartening, but it's hardly a sufficient cause to trim -- or exit altogether -- their positions in Critical Metals. Analysts' opinions vary, and there are potential catalysts on the horizon -- such as the manufacturer's definitive feasibility study -- that are more crucial to monitor.

    Similarly, the shareholder dilution resulting from the acquisition of European Lithium is surely unwelcome, but it may be worthwhile if the manufacturer succeeds in developing the Tanbreez project.

    The swing in Critical Metals stock this week may be disappointing, but volatility like this is typical for growth stocks. For those who are losing sleep over the volatility, however, it may be more comfortable to hold a rare-earth ETF rather than Critical Metals directly.

    • Another week without Kenneth Walker III?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 11 is underway, and we're tracking all of the injuries before game time.

    AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots (bye) | JetsAFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns (bye) | SteelersAFC South: Texans (played Thurs.) | Colts (played Thurs.) | Jaguars | TitansAFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | ChargersNFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | CommandersNFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers (bye) | VikingsNFC South: Falcons (bye) | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers (bye)NFC West: Cardinals | Rams (bye) | 49ers | Seahawks (bye).

    Another week without Kenneth Walker III? It's looking that way for the Kansas City Chiefs.

    Recent findings suggest that after missing Week 10 due to groin tightness, the Chiefs running back has yet to practice this week and is in jeopardy of missing Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals. Should he not be able to go, rookie Emmett Johnson, who rushed for 101 yards and caught two receiving touchdowns last week, will once again take on the starter's role.

    "It's getting better, but with those, you don't wanna do something stupid, right?" Chiefs head coach Andy Reid remarked of Walker. "Put him out there, and it's still bugging him a little bit, but he's feeling a lot better than he was. We'll just see. I mean, it's a day-to-day thing, so we'll just see how it goes.".

    San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) has missed the past three games, but he took a big step this week returning to practice as the team prepares for its Mexico City game against the Minnesota Vikings.

    Evans has not been ruled out for Week 11, but being on the field was an encouraging sign for his impending return.

    "We just want to make sure that we're doing the right thing, and our health and performance team has done a great job leading the process," remarked 49ers general manager John Lynch. "Mike's been doing a great job. He's been frustrated. He wants out there on the field, but he's been a pro.".

    Other Week 11 injuries to monitor:.

    In a recent development, luther Burden III (concussion) has cleared protocol after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit in Week 8 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Chicago Bears wide receiver logged back-to-back full practices on Wednesday and Thursday, a good indication he'll be available against the Latest Orleans Saints. Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons isn't concerned about a knee issue that kept him limited this week. "Like 99 problems, but this ain't one," he remarked.

    Sources indicate that injuries that kept him limited in Wednesday's practice did not keep Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) away from being on the field Thursday. The Raiders' leading receiver exited Sunday's loss to the Seattle Seahawks after just 11 snaps with an ankle matter.

    DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has missed the past three games for the Philadelphia Eagles, but says he's 100% and has felt that way for a while. Smith said he was able to play last week against the Carolina Panthers, but some things are out of his control. "I didn't bust my ass this whole summer, I didn't continue to get up at 4:30 in the morning every day, to come out here and not play," he said. "My focus has been to getting where I was supposed to be.".

    Here's the rest of the Week 11 injury report (players will be added as teams release their reports):.

    WR Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle): OUT.

    #4075. Amid recent banking outages, should you start carrying cash again? Top advisors weigh in

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (837 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Amid recent banking outages, should you start carrying cash again? Top advisors weigh in

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For years, Americans have moved away from using physical U.S.
    • Industry observers note that JPMorgan Chase on Monday reported a technical issue that disrupted some consumer banking services, with ripple effects extending to several major U.S.
    • Those reports came on the heels of separate, widespread challenges with Microsoft Outlook and communication systems used by air traffic control centers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For years, Americans have moved away from using physical U.S. currency in favor of credit, debit and digital payments. But amid the recent outages affecting some consumer banking services, experts say it's wise to revisit cash.

    Industry observers note that JPMorgan Chase on Monday reported a technical issue that disrupted some consumer banking services, with ripple effects extending to several major U.S. banks and the peer-to-peer payments network Zelle. A day later, a separate outage affected Apple, temporarily disrupting Apple Pay and iCloud, the service that keeps data available across various Apple devices.

    Those reports came on the heels of separate, widespread challenges with Microsoft Outlook and communication systems used by air traffic control centers.

    As technology outages expose vulnerabilities across parts of the U.S. economy, some top advisors say consumers should reconsider keeping physical money on hand.

    "This is about preparedness, not panic," said David La Placa, CEO of Intellectus Partners in San Francisco, which ranked No. 92 on CNBC's Financial Advisor 100 list for 2026. "I think keeping some cash at home is a reasonable starting point for many households.".

    La Placa advises consumers to "build redundancy" into their financial lives.

    "Maintain access to at least a second financial institution, keep a backup credit card from a different issuer and make sure you have more than one way to access liquidity," he said.

    A client's cash management should be diversified, mentioned Seth Fierston, a certified financial planner and co-president of Fierston Financial Group in West Hartford, Connecticut. The firm ranked No. 22 on CNBC's Financial Advisor 100 list.

    Industry observers note that having multiple accounts at brokerages or banks and various ways to move money, including Automated Clearing House, or ACH, wire, check, Venmo or Zelle, "can help mitigate technology risk," Fierston said. "One of our guiding principles is flexibility.".

    When it comes to everyday transactions, Americans are increasingly relying on digital forms of payment.

    These days, only about 46% of Americans carry cash with them always or most of the time, according to a survey of nearly 10,000 adults conducted between May and June by the Pew Research Center, a nonpartisan research group.

    Roughly 42% of U.S. adults said they don't use cash for any purchases in a typical week, up from 24% in 2015, Pew found.

    Recent findings suggest that young adults are the least likely to carry physical currency. Among adults under 30, 51% said they go completely cashless, according to the survey.

    According to recent reports, "I recommend to my clients that they always keep three days of average cash spend on hand given the uncertainty of life in general," stated Tim Lootens, CFP, managing director at Chilton Capital Management in Houston, which ranked No. 7 on this year's Financial Advisor 100.

    Considering the recent technical troubles, Lootens mentioned consumers should keep even more cash at the ready.

    "We've had the Microsoft Outlook outage, the FAA ground shutdown and now banking disruption," he said. "This makes me think five to seven days may be a better number.".

    The right amount is as psychological as it is financial, he added. "The ability to access cash and having comfort knowing it is there when needed is so key," he remarked.

    Brian Vendig, president and chief investment officer at MJP Wealth Advisors, which ranked No. 42 on CNBC's Financial Advisor 100, also noted he recommends holding a dollar amount that corresponds with a household's discretionary living expenses. He advised having enough for at least one to two weeks, depending on their needs.

    While there is little precedent for a banking or payment system outage lasting more than a few business days, Vendig stated, a one- to two-week cash reserve provides a "reasonable buffer" for essentials such as groceries, gas and other necessities, if electronic payments become unavailable.

    "We apply this range because it is also an emotional concern for most people, and they might want to have a little extra saved at home due to the size of their household and having a little extra 'peace of mind' guarantee," he said.

    Vendig said he recommends stashing extra cash in a secure location at home for emergency needs.

    Vendig also remarked consumers should be vigilant in ensuring their electronic devices have the most recent software security patches installed.

    Criminals will try to exploit moments of uncertainty, experts say.

    "Consumers should assume they will be targeted," stated Craig Timm, senior director of anti-money laundering at ACAMS, an anti-financial crime group.

    According to recent reports, "[This week's] reported bank outages are likely to cause widespread confusion and fear among consumers about losing access to their money," he remarked. "Criminals will try to exploit that anxiety by pushing victims to take urgent action to protect their funds or restore account access.".

    It has been revealed that as always, "stay alert, never click on links in unexpected bank messages and never share personal information such as passwords or PINs," he advised. "If you need to reach your bank, use a trusted, official channel," Timm remarked.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Payward, the owner of crypto exchange Kraken, is pushing into private markets with its latest acquisition, underscoring a broader shift in cryptocurrencies, from trading-led growth to the buildout of financial infrastructure.
    • Payward stated late Wednesday that it's buying venture capital and asset management provider Tribe Capital Management, led by Payward's co-CEO Arjun Sethi.
    • Tribe, where Sethi is co-founder and chairman, invests across early- and late-stage private companies and has $2.7 billion in assets under management.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Payward, the owner of crypto exchange Kraken, is pushing into private markets with its latest acquisition, underscoring a broader shift in cryptocurrencies, from trading-led growth to the buildout of financial infrastructure.

    Payward stated late Wednesday that it's buying venture capital and asset management provider Tribe Capital Management, led by Payward's co-CEO Arjun Sethi. No purchase price was disclosed.

    Tribe, where Sethi is co-founder and chairman, invests across early- and late-stage private companies and has $2.7 billion in assets under management.

    Recent findings suggest that "Joining Payward gives us the opportunity to bring Tribe's investment approach to a global financial platform," Jonathan Hsu, another co-founder of Tribe Capital, noted in a statement. "We see a strong fit between our investment approach and Payward's infrastructure, distribution, and product-building capabilities.".

    Payward didn't respond to a request for comment.

    The acquisition is novel among crypto exchanges. Unlike exchange-owned venture arms such as Coinbase Ventures or Binance Labs, Payward is looking to integrate Tribe's investment and fund-management capabilities into an existing custody, trading, collateral and tokenization infrastructure to develop private-market investment products.

    Payward is trying to position itself to capture value from a broader crypto-driven transformation of financial services, not use the venture vehicle to draw more capital into the crypto ecosystem.

    In a recent development, the acquisition is another step in the evolution in the crypto exchange business model. With cryptocurrency prices continuing to decline this year, crypto exchanges have worked to move past their reliance on trading volumes and transaction fees, focusing instead on building the infrastructure connecting digital assets with traditional finance.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Liverpool have been handed a significant double injury boost in the days leading up to their Premier League clash against Manchester United.

    Andoni Iraola will be pleased that his players who were on international duty all seem set to return to Merseyside unscathed, even though Dominik Szoboszlai controversially played through the pain barrier for Hungary.

    The Reds’ head coach is still waiting for a handful of long-term injury absentees to become available once more, but two of those have now taken a major step in their respective recoveries.

    As reported by Paul Joyce for The Times, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to Liverpool first-team training, with both defenders having been sidelined for a number of months with serious knee injuries.

    The Northern Ireland right-back has been out of action since January after he was struck down towards the end of the 0-0 draw at Arsenal; while the Italian teenager has been absent for even longer, not playing since rupturing his ACL on his Reds debut in September 2025.

    The latter had been due to resume full training in early October before that staging post was delayed as medical staff took a cautious approach, but he’s now in the final stages of his recovery to full fitness and could resume playing in the coming weeks.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    While we wouldn’t bank on either of the Liverpool duo returning to matchday action in the concluding weeks of 2026, their resumption of first-team training comes as a huge step towards their long-awaited comebacks.

    Bradley would very likely have made the right-back position his own this season had he not been sidelined, but thankfully Ronald Araujo has excelled in that role since joining on loan from Barcelona in August.

    As for Leoni, it was beyond cruel that he tore his ACL towards the end of what had been a terrific Reds debut against Southampton 14 months ago, but he’s still only 19 and should hopefully have a hugely successful career still ahead of him.

    Even when both players are cleared for a return to action, it’ll take time for them to properly get back into a matchday rhythm, and Iraola will surely bed them in gently after missing so much football over the past few months.

    However, having them back in a full training feels like a significant step forward, and when the time comes for them to resume playing, it’ll be a wonderful sight for everyone associated with Liverpool.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • In a recent development, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    In a recent development, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    It has been revealed that securitize reinforced "certain areas of the tech giant like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Recent findings suggest that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    Anthropic IPO 'exactly what the markets need,' but analysts warn of volatility

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's blockbuster IPO on Thursday gave markets a much-needed boost after weeks of weakness, though analysts warned that the stock could remain volatile in the coming weeks.
    • Share of the Claude maker opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 per share, 17% above the IPO price.
    • Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott described investors as "foaming at the mouth" for the offering, with allocations "impossibly low," underscoring the strength of demand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's blockbuster IPO on Thursday gave markets a much-needed boost after weeks of weakness, though analysts warned that the stock could remain volatile in the coming weeks.

    Share of the Claude maker opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 per share, 17% above the IPO price. The offering raised $81.3 billion through the sale of 980 million shares — surpassing SpaceX's June listing to become the largest IPO on record.

    Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott described investors as "foaming at the mouth" for the offering, with allocations "impossibly low," underscoring the strength of demand.

    "Anthropic's IPO is exactly what the markets need to revive overall sentiment," stated Rebecca Walser, chief investment officer at Walser Wealth Management, adding that markets have been "depressed with all of the negativity in the AI complex over the past several weeks.".

    Still, U.S. equities fell sharply on Thursday, with the tech heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25% to end at 23,879.20, S&P 500 down 2.02% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 2.19%.

    Artificial intelligence and technology stocks initially rose thanks to the IPO, but the gains faded as "profit-taking spread across AI-related stocks," noted James Ooi, chief market strategist at Tiger Brokers.

    While the initial pop was not surprising for such a highly anticipated listing, investors should avoid "chasing the IPO," Walser noted.

    She expects the stock to come under pressure in the coming weeks as former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang testifies before the U.S. Senate, potentially reviving concerns around the AI sector.

    "The shares remain highly volatile," said Morningstar senior equity analyst Malik Ahmed Khan.

    Walser noted that any weakness around the time of Huang's testimony could offer an entry point for investors interested in Anthropic, adding that she remains bullish on the OpenAI rival over the long term.

    "For investors, it's going to become a blue-chip stock like Google," Ross Gerber, president and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia.".

    In a recent development, he added that U.S. technology valuations are at ridiculously low levels relative to the "crazy amazing innovation" coming out of California.

    Morningstar's Khan struck a more cautious tone, warning investors against getting swept up in the enthusiasm around Anthropic, advising them instead to step back and "carefully" assess the company as a long-term business.

    That will depend on Anthropic's ability to scale enterprise adoption, continue improving its models and turn those capabilities into economically useful products and services in the AI ecosystem, he said.

    "We remain confident that the firm will be able to execute on all three fronts," Khan added, setting a $92 fair value estimate for the stock.

    Walser stated that Anthropic is "extremely important for the overall AI story" as the first non-Chinese large language model developer to go public.

    Its listing gives public-market investors their first direct test of how a major standalone AI model developer will be valued and perform outside the chip sector. Meanwhile, rival OpenAI could follow with an IPO sometime in 2027.

    "This IPO is the show me moment for the AI story," Walser remarked, as much of the stock market's AI narrative has so far centered on chipmakers.
